title: 10 Years Jail: India's Paper Leak Law Explained #Shorts
description:
India's paper leak law, the Public Examinations Act 2024, carries up to 10 years in jail for organised exam-leak crime. It covers central exams like UPSC, SSC, Railway Recruitment Boards, IBPS and NTA, and the offences are cognisable and non-bailable. Our view is that it puts real jail time behind the promise of fair exams, so what one safeguard would you add?
Subscribe to Sankalp for the government's side of every big story.
Sources: Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 (Act 1 of 2024), India Code; PRS Legislative Research. Wikimedia image credits listed below.
This video is commentary. The anchors and some visuals are AI-made.

SCRIPT:
ROHAN: Ten years in jail. That's the top penalty for organised paper-leak crime in India. [10 YEARS]
KAVYA: It's the Public Examinations Act, 2024. Parliament passed it in February 2024, and it came into force on 21 June 2024.
ROHAN: It covers central public exams: UPSC, SSC, Railway Recruitment Boards, IBPS and NTA. State exams fall under state laws.
KAVYA: Under the Act, using unfair means like leaking papers brings three to five years in jail and a fine up to ₹10 lakh. Organised leak crime: five to ten years, and a fine of at least ₹1 crore.
ROHAN: Exam service providers face a fine up to ₹1 crore, plus the cost of the exam, and a four-year ban from conducting exams.
KAVYA: Here's what most people miss. The offences are cognisable and non-bailable. And the government says the law is aimed mainly at organised gangs and insiders.
ROHAN [OPINION tag on screen]: Our view: this is India's first dedicated central law against paper leaks. It puts real jail time behind the promise of fair exams.
KAVYA: What one safeguard would you add? Tell us in the comments. Follow Sankalp for the government's side of every big story.
